subject.name: Chemistry
subject.description: Grade 11 Semester 1 Chemistry introduces the foundations of chemical thinking, from solutions and water chemistry to acids, rates, equilibrium, and ionic systems. This course develops conceptual understanding of matter, reactions, and quantitative analysis while building the skills needed for scientific problem solving.

content.title: Unit 1 (Lo1)
content.description: This unit introduces the chemistry of solutions, concentration, and water quality, helping students understand how dissolved substances behave in aqueous systems and why these properties are essential in daily life, industry, and environmental science.

concepts.title: Solutions and aqueous solutions
concepts.description: This concept explains the formation of solutions and the special role of water as a universal solvent, showing how substances dissolve and interact in aqueous environments.

concepts.title: Solubility of salts  — temperature impact
concepts.description: This concept explores how temperature changes the solubility of salts and why this relationship is important in chemistry, environmental systems, and industrial processes.

concepts.title: Solubility curves
concepts.description: This concept introduces solubility curves as visual tools for predicting how much solute can dissolve at a given temperature and comparing different substances.

concepts.title: Quantitative analysis
concepts.description: This concept covers methods for measuring concentrations and dissolved substances, emphasizing the importance of precise quantitative analysis in chemistry.

concepts.title: ppm
concepts.description: This concept explains parts per million as a method for expressing very small concentrations, especially in water quality and environmental chemistry.

concepts.title: Molarity
concepts.description: This concept defines molarity as a standard measure of solution concentration and shows how it is calculated and used in chemical calculations.

concepts.title: Molality
concepts.description: This concept explains molality as a concentration unit based on solvent mass and emphasizes its usefulness when temperature changes are involved.

concepts.title: Normality
concepts.description: This concept describes normality as a concentration unit related to reactive equivalents and shows when it is useful in acid-base and redox chemistry.

concepts.title: Mole fraction
concepts.description: This concept introduces mole fraction as a way to express the proportion of each component in a mixture and its connection to solution composition.

concepts.title: Mass percentage
concepts.description: This concept shows how mass percentage is used to describe concentration by mass and why it is widely applied in laboratory and industrial chemistry.

concepts.title: TDS
concepts.description: This concept defines total dissolved solids and explains how they affect water quality, taste, and suitability for human and industrial use.

concepts.title: The different ion percentages which the human body needs daily
concepts.description: This concept examines the essential ions the body requires daily and illustrates how mineral balance supports health, metabolism, and biological function.

concepts.title: Resins
concepts.description: This concept introduces resins as ion-exchange materials used to remove unwanted ions and purify water in analytical and industrial applications.

concepts.title: EDTA  — including ion exchange
concepts.description: This concept explains the role of EDTA in binding metal ions and how ion-exchange principles are used to soften water and separate dissolved contaminants.

concepts.title: Electrodialysis
concepts.description: This concept describes electrodialysis as a process that separates ions using an electric field and membrane technology for water purification.

concepts.title: Reverse osmosis
concepts.description: This concept explains reverse osmosis as a filtration method that removes dissolved salts and impurities by forcing water through a semi-permeable membrane.

concepts.title: Dissolved oxygen  — DO
concepts.description: This concept introduces dissolved oxygen as a critical parameter in water quality and aquatic ecosystems, highlighting its influence on life and environmental health.

content.title: Unit 2 (Lo2)
content.description: This unit explores the unique properties of water and the effects of dissolved solutes on physical properties such as density, conductivity, boiling point, freezing point, and osmotic pressure.

concepts.title: Water in the environment
concepts.description: This concept examines water as a natural resource and a key component of ecosystems, emphasizing its distribution, movement, and importance to life.

concepts.title: Properties and types
concepts.description: This concept reviews the physical and chemical properties of water and distinguishes the main types of water systems relevant to chemistry and environment.

concepts.title: Measuring densities
concepts.description: This concept explains how density is measured and why differences in density help chemists identify materials and understand water behavior.

concepts.title: Conductivity
concepts.description: This concept describes conductivity as the ability of a solution to carry electric current and connects it to ion concentration and electrolyte strength.

concepts.title: pH
concepts.description: This concept introduces pH as a measure of acidity or alkalinity and shows how it influences chemical reactions, water quality, and living systems.

concepts.title: Boiling points
concepts.description: This concept examines how the boiling point of a solution changes with composition and explains the effect of solute concentration on thermal behavior.

concepts.title: Effect of solutes on physical properties
concepts.description: This concept explains how dissolved substances alter physical properties such as boiling point, melting point, and vapor pressure in solution systems.

concepts.title: Colligative properties
concepts.description: This concept introduces colligative properties as solution properties that depend on the number of dissolved particles rather than the identity of the solute.

concepts.title: Elevation in B.P.
concepts.description: This concept explains boiling point elevation as a result of dissolved particles lowering the solvent’s tendency to escape into the vapor phase.

concepts.title: Depression in F.P.
concepts.description: This concept shows how freezing point depression occurs when solutes disrupt crystal formation, lowering the temperature at which a liquid freezes.

concepts.title: Osmotic pressure
concepts.description: This concept explains osmotic pressure as the force that drives solvent movement across a semi-permeable membrane and highlights its importance in biology and chemistry.

content.title: Unit 3 (Lo3)
content.description: This unit develops the acid-base foundation of chemistry by examining acids, bases, pH, salt behavior, and the structural factors that determine whether a substance acts as an acid or base.

concepts.title: Acids
concepts.description: This concept introduces acids as substances that donate protons or increase hydrogen ion concentration in solution and explains their common chemical behavior.

concepts.title: Nature of acids
concepts.description: This concept explains the chemical nature of acids, including their ionization, proton donation, and relationship to molecular structure.

concepts.title: Acid strength
concepts.description: This concept describes how acid strength depends on ionization and the stability of the conjugate base, helping students compare strong and weak acids.

concepts.title: pH scale
concepts.description: This concept introduces the pH scale as a logarithmic measure of acidity and alkalinity and shows how it relates to hydrogen ion concentration.

concepts.title: Polyprotic acid
concepts.description: This concept explains polyprotic acids as acids that can donate more than one proton and shows how successive ionizations affect chemical behavior.

concepts.title: Bases
concepts.description: This concept defines bases as substances that accept protons or produce hydroxide ions in solution and highlights their role in neutralization reactions.

concepts.title: Acid-base properties of salts
concepts.description: This concept explores how salts can behave as acidic, basic, or neutral substances depending on the ions they release in water.

concepts.title: Effect of structure on acid-base properties
concepts.description: This concept shows how molecular structure and electron distribution influence whether a compound acts as an acid or a base in chemical reactions.

concepts.title: Acid-base properties of oxides
concepts.description: This concept explains how oxides can act as acidic or basic compounds depending on their composition and the chemical environment they are placed in.

concepts.title: The Lewis Acid-Base Model
concepts.description: This concept introduces the Lewis model, which defines acids and bases by electron-pair donation and acceptance, expanding the concept beyond proton transfer.

content.title: Unit 4 (Lo4)
content.description: This unit focuses on the fundamentals of reaction kinetics, introducing the language of chemical reactions, rate measurement, and the mathematical relationship between reactant concentration and reaction speed.

concepts.title: Order
concepts.description: This concept explains the order of a reaction as the dependence of the rate on reactant concentration and how it is determined experimentally.

concepts.title: Molecularity
concepts.description: This concept defines molecularity as the number of reacting particles involved in an elementary step and distinguishes it from reaction order.

concepts.title: Rate of chemical reaction
concepts.description: This concept introduces reaction rate as the change in concentration over time and highlights its importance in understanding how fast chemical processes occur.

concepts.title: Law of mass action
concepts.description: This concept explains the law of mass action, which connects reaction rate to the concentrations of reactants and provides the basis for rate equations.

concepts.title: Determination of rate of reaction
concepts.description: This concept examines the methods used to determine reaction rate experimentally and shows how rate data can be analyzed for chemical insight.

content.title: Unit 5 (Lo5)
content.description: This unit examines how reaction rate can be changed by catalysts and activation energy, helping students connect kinetic theory with the practical factors that influence chemical processes.

concepts.title: Catalyst
concepts.description: This concept explains how catalysts increase reaction rate by lowering the activation energy without being consumed in the reaction itself.

concepts.title: Activation energy
concepts.description: This concept introduces activation energy as the minimum energy required for a reaction to occur and shows why it controls reaction speed.

concepts.title: Effects of different variables on the rate of chemical reaction
concepts.description: This concept explores how changing variables such as concentration, temperature, surface area, and catalysts affects the speed of chemical reactions.

content.title: Unit 6 (Lo6)
content.description: This unit introduces chemical equilibria, showing that many reactions do not go to completion and instead settle into dynamic balance governed by reversible processes and equilibrium constants.

concepts.title: Chemical equilibria
concepts.description: This concept explains chemical equilibrium as the state in which the forward and reverse reaction rates are equal, creating a stable balance in a reversible system.

concepts.title: Reversible reactions
concepts.description: This concept examines reversible reactions and how the system can proceed in both directions until equilibrium is reached.

concepts.title: Dynamic equilibrium
concepts.description: This concept explains dynamic equilibrium as a state of constant microscopic change with no net macroscopic change in concentrations.

concepts.title: Factors affecting chemical equilibria
concepts.description: This concept explores how concentration, pressure, temperature, and catalysts influence the position of equilibrium in a reaction mixture.

concepts.title: Equilibrium graphing
concepts.description: This concept introduces equilibrium graphs as visual tools for understanding how reactant and product concentrations change as a system approaches balance.

concepts.title: Equilibrium constants
concepts.description: This concept defines equilibrium constants and explains how they quantify the ratio of product to reactant concentrations at equilibrium.

concepts.title: The Haber process
concepts.description: This concept examines the Haber process as a major industrial method for making ammonia and shows how equilibrium principles guide industrial chemistry.

concepts.title: The Contact process
concepts.description: This concept introduces the Contact process as an industrial method for producing sulfuric acid and emphasizes the importance of equilibrium conditions in manufacturing.

content.title: Unit 7 (Lo7)
content.description: This unit develops ionic equilibria and acid-base theory, focusing on pH, buffer systems, weak acid/base behavior, and the chemical principles behind solubility and equilibrium in ionic systems.

concepts.title: Ionic equilibria
concepts.description: This concept explains ionic equilibria as the balance established when ions dissolve and react in solution, which is central to acid-base and solubility chemistry.

concepts.title: Brønsted-Lowry theory of acids and bases
concepts.description: This concept introduces the Brønsted-Lowry theory, defining acids as proton donors and bases as proton acceptors in solution.

concepts.title: Acid dissociation constants, Ka and the use of pKa
concepts.description: This concept defines Ka and pKa as tools for comparing acid strength and understanding how weak acids dissociate in water.

concepts.title: The ionic product of water, Kw
concepts.description: This concept explains the ionic product of water and how it underpins the relationship between hydrogen and hydroxide ion concentrations in aqueous solutions.

concepts.title: pH: choice of pH indicators
concepts.description: This concept shows how pH indicators work by changing color over a specific range and how the correct indicator is chosen for a titration or acid-base analysis.

concepts.title: Buffer solutions
concepts.description: This concept explains buffer solutions as systems that resist pH change when small amounts of acid or base are added, which is important in biological and laboratory systems.

concepts.title: Solubility product
concepts.description: This concept introduces the solubility product as the equilibrium constant for a sparingly soluble salt and shows how it predicts precipitation behavior.

concepts.title: The common ion effect
concepts.description: This concept explains how adding a common ion reduces the solubility of a sparingly soluble salt and demonstrates the influence of equilibrium on dissolution.

content.title: Midterm Revisions
content.description: A focused review of the major ideas, equations, and practical skills introduced in the first half of the course, designed to strengthen conceptual recall and exam readiness.

content.title: Final Revisions
content.description: A final consolidation of the most important chemistry ideas and problem-solving strategies from the semester, preparing students for cumulative assessment and long-term understanding.
